title: Xia et al. 2022 — Topical Skin Delivery Suitability Report
paperTitle: Nanoliposome Use to Improve the Stability of Phenylethyl Resorcinol and Serve as a Skin Penetration Enhancer for Skin Whitening
metadata:
Authors: Huan Xia et al.
Journal: Coatings 12, 362 (2022)
Published: 9 March 2022
DOI: 10.3390/coatings12030362
summaryCaution: Strong single-active whitening case, but skin delivery is inferred from FITC imaging rather than quantitative PR recovery or an in-vivo whitening study.

criteria.reported: Original formulation, stability, release, cell and pig-skin experiments are reported.
criteria.interesting: Links carrier work to a cosmetic-active endpoint.
criteria.caution: All efficacy evidence remains in vitro.

criteria.reported: PR is identified as a tyrosinase inhibitor with poor solubility and photostability.
criteria.assessment: Identity and delivery liabilities are clear, but a full physicochemical profile is not supplied.
criteria.interesting: One defined active, not a botanical mixture.
criteria.caution: No pKa, logP or numerical solubility is reported.
criteria.missing: Need reliable database values and conditions.

criteria.reported: Poor solubility and UVA instability limit PR use; the study targets skin whitening.
criteria.assessment: The topical-delivery problem is explicit and relevant.
criteria.interesting: Photostability is a genuine secondary product problem.
criteria.caution: The relative importance of each limitation is not quantified.

criteria.reported: PR inhibits tyrosinase; PR and PR-NLP reduce cellular tyrosinase activity and melanin in B16F10 cells.
criteria.assessment: Mechanism and epidermal-melanocyte target are coherent.
criteria.interesting: Carrier gives a stronger cellular effect than PR solution at tested doses.
criteria.caution: B16F10 cells do not prove human skin whitening.
criteria.missing: No human melanocyte, reconstructed-skin or clinical efficacy data.

criteria.reported: The paper identifies stratum corneum as the main penetration barrier and uses pig skin.
criteria.assessment: Barrier rationale is relevant to lipid nanoliposomes.
criteria.interesting: Pig skin is a more relevant model than rodent skin for this purpose.
criteria.caution: No skin-integrity acceptance criterion is reported.

criteria.reported: Ethanol-injection nanoliposomes include phospholipid, cholesterol, Tween 80 and DHHB; optimized size is 130.1 ± 3.54 nm.
criteria.assessment: A conventional but well-characterized lipid nanocarrier.
criteria.interesting: DHHB is included to improve PR photostability.

criteria.reported: Encapsulation, lipid affinity and small particle size are proposed to protect PR and improve entry; release, uptake and imaging are measured.
criteria.assessment: The proposed chain fits the active’s problems, with partial mechanistic evidence.
criteria.interesting: Photoprotection and delivery are addressed in one system.
criteria.caution: FITC is a surrogate, not PR.
criteria.missing: Need quantitative PR distribution and carrier fate in skin.

criteria.reported: Pig-skin Franz cells compare FITC solution and FITC-PR-NLP over 4–24 h; cryosections are imaged by CLSM.
criteria.assessment: Useful qualitative penetration experiment, not a full quantitative permeation study.
criteria.interesting: Time-resolved cross-sections visually show deeper signal for carrier.
criteria.caution: The test substitutes FITC for PR and removes skin at each time point.
criteria.missing: No PR receptor amount, flux, retention, mass balance, n or statistics stated for this assay.

criteria.reported: Dialysis release compares equal PR dose in PR-NLPs and PR ethanol solution; 12 h values are 29.90 ± 4.05% and 94.21 ± 2.31%.
criteria.assessment: Conditions, control and long 72 h profile support sustained release.
criteria.interesting: The contrast makes the formulation effect easy to teach.
criteria.caution: The method inconsistently states 0.1% and 1% Tween 80.
criteria.missing: No membrane-area or release-model analysis reported.

criteria.reported: Free PR solution, blank NLPs and PR-NLPs are used across relevant assays.
criteria.assessment: Controls are generally good for formulation and cell effects.
criteria.interesting: Blank NLPs contribute to cytotoxicity interpretation.
criteria.caution: Skin experiment is FITC solution versus FITC carrier, not PR formulation versus PR solution.
criteria.missing: No matched cosmetic vehicle or commercial comparator.

criteria.reported: Size, PDI, zeta potential, EE, loading and cumulative release are reported.
criteria.assessment: Formulation quantification is strong; skin-delivery quantification is weak.
criteria.caution: Fluorescence-depth images cannot yield PR flux or deposition.
criteria.missing: Need cumulative PR, Jss, Kp, lag time and layer recovery.

criteria.reported: Single-factor and Box–Behnken optimization, triplicate stability, characterization, cytotoxicity and stated t tests are included.
criteria.assessment: Broad design gives credible proof of concept.
criteria.interesting: Three-month physical and chemical stability at 4 and 25 °C in dark is reported.
criteria.caution: Photostability is not a finished-product photostability protocol.
criteria.missing: No sample-size rationale, human model or skin-assay validation.

criteria.reported: The evidence contains a clear, consequential gap between imaging and quantitative delivery claims.
criteria.assessment: Excellent discussion paper because the critique is specific and fair.
criteria.interesting: Fig.11 supports entry but not the conclusion of improved PR permeation through skin.
criteria.caution: Critique potential is not experimental quality.

criteria.reported: Specific weaknesses identify feasible next experiments.
criteria.assessment: Several alternative approaches can be compared without changing the whitening objective.
criteria.interesting: Epidermal retention may be preferable to transdermal escape for a whitening active.

criteria.reported: PR-NLPs show cell compatibility at useful concentrations, UV/three-month stability and whitening-relevant cellular effects.
criteria.assessment: A credible early cosmetic-delivery case, not product proof.
criteria.interesting: Single compound and a concrete photostability issue make it class-friendly.
criteria.caution: No human irritation, sensitization, phototoxicity, preservative, packaging or sensory evidence.
criteria.missing: Need cosmetic safety and manufacturing package.

sections.summary:
This paper packages the single whitening active phenylethyl resorcinol (PR) in nanoliposomes to address poor solubility and UVA instability. It provides a strong formulation-to-cell-efficacy story, including sustained release, stability, cell uptake, tyrosinase and melanin assays.

The decisive limitation is that the skin study visualizes FITC-labelled carrier, not quantitatively assayed PR. It supports skin entry but cannot establish PR flux, retention or mass balance. Interpretation is this review’s assessment, not an author claim.

Evidence scope: Full PDF extracted once with MarkItDown; Methods, Results, Tables and Figs. 5, 10 and 11 reviewed. No supplement identified. Reviewed 8 September 2026.
sections.logic:
1 API

PR, single tyrosinase inhibitor.

2 Problem

Poor solubility and UVA instability.

3 Barrier

Stratum corneum limits epidermal delivery.

4 System

~130 nm lipid nanoliposome.

5 Expected

Protect PR, sustain release, improve entry.

6 Observed

Release, cell effects and deeper FITC signal; quantitative PR skin delivery missing.
sections.design:
Question: can PR-NLP improve PR stability and topical whitening-relevant delivery?

ComponentAssessment
OptimizationSingle-factor plus Box–Behnken formulation optimization.

sections.permeation:
ParameterPaper condition / critique
ModelFresh full-thickness dorsal pig skin, Franz cell, 2 cm diffusion diameter [Section 2.8].
Dose/receptor4 mL FITC solution or FITC-PR-NLP; 20 mL 10% ethanol/PBS, 37 ± 0.5 °C, 450 rpm.
ReadoutCLSM 10 µm sections at 4–24 h; appropriate for location, insufficient for PR flux.
MissingNo PR assay, receptor samples, integrity test, mass balance, n or statistics reported.
sections.release:
PR-NLPs and equal PR ethanol solution were placed in 8–14 kDa dialysis bags; receptor was 400 mL PBS pH 6.8 with Tween 80, 37 ± 0.5 °C and 100 rpm. One mL samples were replaced [Section 2.4.7]. PR-NLP release was 29.90 ± 4.05% at 12 h versus 94.21 ± 2.31% for solution and approached equilibrium at 72 h [Fig.6].

Score impact: Good comparator and profile; conflicting 0.1%/1% Tween wording and dialysis limitations reduce certainty.
sections.data:
ResultInterpretation / gap
Carrier130.1 ± 3.54 nm, PDI 0.225 ± 0.02, zeta −43.9 ± 3.44 mV [Table 3].
ReleaseSustained release is demonstrated, but dialysis is not skin permeation [Fig.6].
SkinFig.11 shows deeper FITC signal; it cannot support a numerical enhancement claim for PR.
sections.strengths:
Single active

PR keeps mechanism and formulation discussion focused.

Orthogonal evidence

Stability, release, uptake and B16F10 outcomes are connected.

Relevant skin model

Pig-skin microscopy is a sensible qualitative screen.
sections.critique:
Surrogate mismatch

FITC behaviour is not PR behaviour; quantify PR in donor, skin layers and receptor.

Not a mass balance

Images do not provide flux, Kp, deposition or recovery.

No in-vivo whitening

Cell melanin reduction does not establish cosmetic efficacy.

Release ambiguity

Tween concentration is inconsistent between sentences.

sections.topical:
Advantages

Photostability and sustained release fit topical PR.

Concerns

Carrier safety and efficacy are not demonstrated in humans.

Gaps

No irritation, sensitization, phototoxicity, packaging or scale data.

Applicability

Good teaching case; not finished cosmetic-product evidence.
sections.presentation:
Main critique: distinguish carrier-associated fluorescence from quantitative delivery of PR. Present Fig.6 for sustained release, Fig.10 for the biological mechanism and Fig.11 to explain exactly what imaging can and cannot establish.

Obtain next: reliable PR pKa/logP/solubility, validated human-skin PR mass balance, epidermal/dermal recovery, human melanocyte or reconstructed-pigment-skin efficacy and irritation data.
sections.verdict:
Recommendation: chooseable, with a delivery-evidence caveat

  • Directly fits a single-compound cosmetic whitening topic.
  • Strong physicochemical, photostability, release and cellular evidence.
  • Fig.11 is visually compelling but not quantitative PR permeation evidence.
  • Best used to propose a rigorous epidermal-retention and mass-balance study.
